title: Pipes: small tools in a chain
summary: Send one command's output into the next one, and watch the data change at each step.

text: A pipe | plugs the stdout of one command into the stdin of the next.
- ls prints the file names. Into a pipe, it writes one per line.
- wc -l counts lines. Together: how many files are here?
- Nothing is written to disk in between.
Let's build a real chain, step by step: which errors happen most in app.log?
- Step 1: grep keeps only the lines that contain error.
- Step 2: sort puts the lines in order.
- The result: identical lines are now side by side.
- Step 3: uniq -c merges identical lines that follow each other, and writes how many there were.
Three small tools, one job each, and you can see that disk errors are the most common.

scheme: error disk      ──▶  1 error disk   counted twice
text: Why sort first? uniq only compares a line with the one just before it.
- The two error disk lines are not neighbours, so uniq counts them apart.
- Rule of thumb: sort always comes before uniq.
One more step turns the counts into a top 3:
$ grep error app.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3
- sort -rn sorts by number (-n), biggest first (-r).
Build a pipe the same way: run the first command, look, then add one step at a time.
